speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Inability to pass meconium, Abdominal distension. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Migraine is an impossible diagnosis for an infant with bilious vomiting and abdominal distension; this presentation strongly suggests a mechanical bowel obstruction like Hirschsprung's disease or meconium ileus. I need to see the abdominal X-ray results immediately to evaluate for dilated bowel loops or the "double bubble" sign. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dilated loops of bowel with no gas in the rectum, suggestive of a distal obstruction.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the X-ray findings of dilated bowel loops and no rectal gas, I suspect Hirschsprung's disease. To confirm this, I need to know if a rectal biopsy has been performed or if you can arrange for one immediately. REQUEST TEST: Rectal_Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Absence of ganglion cells in the submucosa and myenteric plexus, consistent with Hirschsprung’s disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: The absence of ganglion cells confirms the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung's disease
